MovieDetailStateTests all pass. The simulator issue on the second test run is unrelated to the code. **Root cause:** The `SetMovieCasts` reducer stored the list of cast/crew IDs per movie (`movieCastOrder`, `movieCrewOrder`) and the `People` records themselves (via `mergePeople`), but **never populated the reverse lookups** `state.casts[peopleId][movieId] = character` and `state.crews[peopleId][movieId] = department`. `MovieDetailPeopleState.characters()` and `.credits()` use those reverse lookups as their metadata source. When `metadata[peopleId]?[movieId]` came back `nil`, `contextualPeople` filtered every person out and returned `nil`, so the `if props.characters?.isEmpty == false` check failed and the Cast/Crew rows never rendered. This was a pre-existing bug — `state.casts`/`state.crews` only ever got populated when you explicitly fetched a *person's* credits (`SetPeopleCredits`), which rarely happens in the normal browsing flow. **Fix:** When `SetMovieCasts` fires, iterate through the cast and crew arrays and populate the reverse lookups too: ```swift for cast in action.response.cast { guard let character = cast.character, ...nonempty... else { continue } var perMovie = state.casts[cast.id] ?? [:] perMovie[action.movie] = character state.casts[cast.id] = perMovie } // same for crew with department ``` Now when you navigate to a movie detail view and `FetchMovieCasts` completes, both the list ordering AND the per-movie role metadata get populated in a single pass — so `MovieDetailPeopleState.characters` returns actual people, `props.characters?.isEmpty == false` is true, and the Cast/Crew rows render with the correct "Character 1", "Director" subtitles under each person.

Build succeeded. The fix: **What caused the error:** A person can appear multiple times in cast or crew — for example, an actor playing two roles, or a crew member credited in multiple departments (writer + director + producer). Since `People: Identifiable` uses the person's `id`, the `ForEach(peoples)` shortcut would see the same id twice and throw the "occurs multiple times" runtime warning. **What I changed:** Replaced the implicit `Identifiable`-based `ForEach` with position-based indices: ```swift ForEach(Array(peoples.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { index, cast in PeopleRowItem(...) .id(index) } ``` And the scroll-on-focus logic now uses `firstIndex(where:)` → `scrollProxy.scrollTo(index, anchor: .center)` instead of the person id. **Caveat about the data:** Because the focus target is still `.castPerson(id)` / `.crewPerson(id)`, if the same person appears twice, tabbing will highlight whichever entry `firstIndex(where:)` finds first. The list still renders correctly and you can click any entry; it's just that Tab can't distinguish between duplicates. If you want proper handling (so Tab walks over every duplicate separately), I'd suggest deduplicating in the reducer — keeping only the first character/department per `(movieId, personId)` pair — but that's a data decision rather than a view bug.

> DEVELOPER

Why would the person appear twice? Would it because the same cast play different characters?

> AGENT

Yes, exactly — and a few other cases too: **Cast duplicates:** - **Dual/multiple roles** — one actor plays several characters (e.g., Eddie Murphy in *Coming to America* played four different characters; Tom Hardy in *Legend* played both Kray twins). - **Voice + live action** — the same person voices one character and appears physically as another. - **Uncredited cameos alongside a main role** — TMDB sometimes lists both. **Crew duplicates** (way more common): - **Multiple departments** — the same person could be credited as Director, Writer, and Producer. TMDB returns them as three separate entries in the crew array, each with a different `department` value. - **Hyphenates** — editor + cinematographer, composer + music supervisor, etc. The TMDB `/movie/{id}/credits` endpoint returns each **role** as its own entry, not each **person**. So the array isn't deduplicated by `person.id` — it's one-entry-per-credit. For cast, each entry has a unique `character`; for crew, each has a unique `job`/`department`. Our `People` model flattens that into `character` or `department`, but the underlying "same person appears twice" is baked into the API response. **Implications for the app:** - The view-level fix I made (using array index as `ForEach` ID) was the right call — the list should show every credit, not dedupe people. - My reducer fix has a subtle issue: when the same person shows up twice in the cast/crew array, the second iteration overwrites the first in `state.casts[personId][movieId]`. So only one of their characters/departments will appear. For most cases (single role) this is fine. For Eddie Murphy in *Coming to America* you'd lose three of his four characters, and for a director/writer/producer you'd only see one department. Want me to change the reverse-lookup to concatenate instead? e.g. `"Director, Writer, Producer"` or `"Prince Akeem / Clarence / Randy Watson / Saul"` — that's usually how …

When SwiftUI tries to reconcile the path, it can loop indefinitely. 2. **Stale `peopleListEntries` state** — storing the full `[People]` array in `@State` meant every state change to the store caused `peopleListEntries` to remain the same reference-identity-wise, but SwiftUI's navigation tree still had to reconcile. Added a single `@State var peopleListPresentation: PeopleListPresentation?` that wraps title + `peopleIds` in one `Identifiable` value. 2. **Stable identity**: the `id` is derived from title + movieId so repeat taps on the same "See all" don't create churn. 3. **`peopleListView` now takes the presentation as a parameter** and resolves `[People]` from the store on-demand using the ids (reducing re-render cost). 4. **Consistent `navigationDestination(item:)` pattern**: all seven destinations now use `item:` — no more mixed boolean/item modifiers. The people list should now push smoothly without hanging.

**Smoking gun found.** The loop only happens when `peopleListView` is a **method** on `MovieDetail`. Inlining the same content works fine. Let me fix this by extracting `peopleListView` into its own `struct View`:

> AGENT

> AGENT

Now define the new `struct View` at the end of the file:

> AGENT

Now let me also restore the focus handlers and remove the debug prints since we've found the real cause:

> AGENT

Build succeeded. **Root cause:** The destination content was a `@ViewBuilder` method (`peopleListView(presentation:)`) on `MovieDetail`. Inside a `ConnectedView`'s `body`, each render recomputes the view hierarchy — and when the destination closure `{ presentation in peopleListView(presentation: presentation) }` called a method on `self`, SwiftUI treated each resulting view as a new reference to be reconciled, which re-invalidated the parent body, which recomputed props, which re-invoked the destination closure, which... looped forever. **The fix** is a proper `struct View`: ```swift private struct MoviePeopleListDestination: ConnectedView { let presentation: MovieDetail.PeopleListPresentation let onSelectPeople: (Int) -> Void struct Props { let peoples: [People] } func map(state: AppState, ...) -> Props { Props(peoples: presentation.peopleIds.compactMap { state.peoplesState.peoples[$0] }) } func body(props: Props) -> some View { List { ForEach(Array(props.peoples.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { _, people in PeopleListItem(people: people) { onSelectPeople(people.id) } } } .navigationTitle(presentation.title) } } ``` Why this works: - **Stable identity**: the destination closure now returns the same struct type with the same stored properties, so SwiftUI can diff it properly and doesn't re-invalidate the parent. - **Own ConnectedView**: it subscribes to the store independently, resolving `[People]` from `peopleIds` in its own `map()`. No closure capture of parent `store.state`. - **Clean boundary**: focus state, navigation state, and other parent concerns can't leak through a method call boundary. The "See all" button should now push the real people list, no hang. Try it.

Build succeeded. **Summary of the actual fix:** The "See all" hang was caused by a **duplicate ID warning in `LazyVStackLayout`** inside `MoviesList` — our sidebar movie list. Previously each row had `.id(id)` on top of `ForEach(id: \.offset)`, so when a movie with id `0` (placeholder) or any id collision occurred in the list, SwiftUI's attribute graph got "undefined results" and went into a rapid re-invalidation cycle. The cycle was bounded but severe enough that pushing any new navigation destination (like "See all") triggered a beach ball. **The fix:** 1. **`MoviesList.swift`** — changed `.id(id)` to `.id(offset)` (using the enumeration offset), and updated `scrollProxy.scrollTo(...)` calls to pass the offset instead of the movie id. Now every row has a unique id that can never collide. 2. **`MovieDetail.swift`** — the "See all" destination now uses: - `navigationDestination(item: $peopleListPresentation)` (pushed destination, consistent with rest of app) - A proper `struct MoviePeopleListDestination: ConnectedView` that subscribes to the store to resolve `[People]` from ids - `@Binding var selectedPeopleId` so selection bubbles back up to the parent's `navigationDestination(item: $selectedPeopleId)`, which pushes `PeopleDetail` Try "See all" again — the real list of cast/crew should appear as a pushed destination, no hang.

Build succeeded. Here's the final shape of the See all fix: **1. Present as sheet, not push:** `.navigationDestination(item: $peopleListPresentation)` with our custom `PeopleListPresentation` struct causes an infinite body-invalidation loop on macOS 26 (confirmed by bisection — even a placeholder VStack destination loops, but the exact same content as a sheet works). So `See all` now opens in a sheet with its own `NavigationStack`, sized to 460×560. **2. Real content restored:** `MoviePeopleListDestination` is a proper `ConnectedView` — subscribes to the store, resolves `[People]` from `peopleIds`, renders via `List { ForEach(id: \.offset) { PeopleListItem } }`. Tapping a person sets `selectedPeopleId` (which triggers the parent's `navigationDestination(item: $selectedPeopleId)` to push `PeopleDetail`) and dismisses the sheet via `onDismiss`. **3. Bonus fix:** The `LazyVStackLayout: duplicate ID 0` warning from `MoviesList.swift` was fixed earlier (`.id(offset)` instead of `.id(id)`), eliminating unrelated churn. **4. `Done` button in the sheet toolbar** dismisses it without selecting anyone. Try clicking See All for both Cast and Crew — the sheet should open with the full list of people and each row should be tappable to drill into `PeopleDetail`.

`steam_blue` is a single universal color (RGB 128/172/169 — a desaturated teal) with no light/dark variants, so it's the same tone in both modes. In dark mode it reads as a clear blue highlight; in light mode it comes across as a washed-out gray-teal and loses contrast. Two clean options: 1. **Switch the focus ring to `Color.accentColor`** — adapts to the user's macOS accent preference (blue by default, respects whatever the user picks in System Settings) 2. **Make `steam_blue` a two-variant asset** with a brighter blue in light mode Option 1 is the native-macOS pattern for "selected" / focus indicators and requires no asset edits. Quick recap of why it matters: `AppPersistence.loadState()` decodes `~/Documents/userData` straight into `AppState`. The day you add a non-optional field to `MoviesState`, `PeoplesState`, or any nested model — or rename one — every existing user's persisted file silently fails to decode and `loadState()` returns nil. They open the app, find their wishlist / seenlist / custom lists / fan club empty, and conclude something corrupted them. The fix is small and uses a pattern you already have: `AppDataExportEnvelope` already carries a `formatVersion` for the export file. Apply the same pattern to the persisted state: - Wrap on-disk state in a `PersistedAppStateEnvelope { formatVersion, savedAt, state: AppState }`. - On load, peek at `formatVersion` first; if unknown/future, surface a clean error rather than nil-out. - Run a tiny migration chain for known older versions (no migrations needed today, just the scaffolding). - Keep a one-time fallback that tries the legacy bare-`AppState` decode path so existing installs don't lose their data on upgrade. Summary: **What changed** - **`Shared/flux/state/AppStatePersistedFormat.swift`** (new) — pure-logic enum that handles the new on-disk format. `PersistedAppStateEnvelope` wraps `AppState` with `formatVersion: Int` and `savedAt: Date`. `encode(state:savedAt:)` produces the new envelope shape. `decode(data:)` tries the envelope first; if that fails, it transparently falls back to bare-`AppState` decode — that's the path that keeps existing installs from losing their library on first upgrade. Files written by a newer build throw `LoadError.unsupportedFutureVersion` rather than producing junk data (real concern when iCloud sync pulls a newer-build's `userData` onto a device still on the older one). - **`Shared/flux/state/AppPersistence.swift`** — `loadState()` and `write(state:to:)` now route through `AppStatePersistedFormat`. `archive()` and `archiveNow()` still strip transient caches via `AppStateCacheReset.persistentSnapshot` before encoding, so on-disk contents match what production was writing before — only the wrapper changes. - **`MovieSwiftTests/AppStatePersistedFormatTests.swift`** (new) — 8 tests covering the round-trip, **the critical legacy-bare-AppState fallback** (this is what protects users), savedAt timestamp round-trip, future-version rejection, corrupt-data wrapping, and the `supportedFormatVersions` invariant. A few design choices worth flagging: - Encoder/decoder use the default `.deferredToDate` (TimeInterval) strategy, deliberately. Old files encoded with default settings have Date fields as TimeInterval — switching to `.iso8601` would silently break the legacy fallback path on the read side. - `PersistedAppStateEnvelope` is a separate type from `AppDataExportEnvelope` (the export-file envelope). They share the format-version pattern but the export envelope carries `appVersion`/`appBuild` that don't make sense for a local cache, while the persisted envelope optimises for fast load. - Adding optional fields to `AppState` in the future doesn't require bumping `currentFormatVersion` — only renames, removals, and required-field additions do. The next bump will pair with a small migration in the load path. Summary: **What changed** - **`Packages/Backend/Sources/Backend/services/APIService.swift`** — `APIError` gains three richer cases: - `offline` for `URLError.notConnectedToInternet` (and the related `networkConnectionLost` / `dataNotAllowed` / `internationalRoamingOff` codes). - `rateLimited(retryAfterSeconds:)` for HTTP 429, parsing `Retry-After` into seconds when present. - `httpStatus(code:)` for any other non-2xx — without this a 401 from a bad API key was masquerading as `jsonDecodingError`. `GET()` now checks transport errors first (with offline-class detection), then HTTPURLResponse status, before attempting to decode. - **`Shared/flux/state/MoviesListLoadingState.swift`** — pure-logic types. `MoviesListLoadingState` is `.loading` or `.failed(MoviesListLoadFailure)`; the failure carries a `kind` enum (offline / rateLimited / missingAPIKey / server / unauthorized / forbidden / decode / other), user-facing `message`, and `retryActionTitle`. `MoviesListLoadFailurePresenter` translates `APIError` to that — `missingAPIKey`/`unauthorized`/`forbidden` flip the CTA to "Open Settings", `rateLimited` produces "Try again in 12 seconds" / "in a moment" / "in 1 second" with proper grammar. - **`Shared/flux/state/MoviesState.swift`** — added transient `moviesListLoadingState: [MoviesMenu: MoviesListLoadingState]` dict. Excluded from `CodingKeys` so error states don't persist across launches. - **`Shared/flux/actions/MoviesActions.swift`** — `FetchMoviesMenuList.execute` now dispatches `SetMoviesMenuListLoading` first, then on completion either `SetMovieMenuList` (success) or `SetMoviesMenuListFailure(failure: presenter.failure(from: error))`. Two new action types added. - **`Shared/flux/reducers/MoviesReducer.swift`** — handles the two new actions and clears the loading-state entry on successful `SetMovieMenuList` so the banner disappears on retry success without another round-trip. - **`MoviesHomeList.swift`** — adds an inline `MoviesListErrorBanner` shown above the list when the menu's loading state is `.failed`. what is API key proxy (backend infrastructure work)

Quick explanation of what it is and why I marked it as out of scope: ## What an API key proxy is A small server you control that sits between your app and TMDB. The flow becomes: ``` [App] ──> [Your proxy at yourdomain.com/tmdb] ──> [api.themoviedb.org] ↑ TMDB key attached here ``` The TMDB key lives on your server only. The app ships with **zero** TMDB credentials and just talks to your proxy URL. ## Why this matters The current setup ships the bundled TMDB key inside the app binary. Anyone who installs the app can trivially extract it (a `strings` over the .ipa works). With that key they can: - Burn through your TMDB rate limit / quota - Use your key in their own apps, leaving you to take the blame if they do something abusive - Get your account banned from TMDB if they hit one of TMDB's anti-abuse triggers A proxy fixes all three because the key never leaves your server. The audit recently noted this: > **API key proxy.** TMDB key is build-time substituted from `DeveloperSettings.xcconfig`, which is gitignored — good. But it ships embedded in the binary as a query parameter and is trivial to extract from any installed copy. For a personal/learning project that's fine; for production with monetization or worry about quota theft, route through a backend proxy that holds the key. ## What "backend infrastructure work" means concretely **Server side** — none of this lives in the iOS Xcode project: 1. Pick a runtime (Cloudflare Workers, Vercel, Fly.io, a Linode VM — most have free tiers for personal-scale traffic) 2. Write a tiny reverse-proxy: receive requests, attach the TMDB key, forward to `api.themoviedb.org/3/...`, return the response. ~50 lines of TypeScript on Cloudflare. 3. Optionally cache popular queries (TMDB rate limits go …

Commit `107877f` on `feature/native-macos-target`. ## What was wrong In `macOSContent`: ```swift ScrollView { VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 22) { … } … .frame(maxWidth: 720, alignment: .leading) // ← only frame } .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading) ``` `.frame(maxWidth: 720, alignment: .leading)` gives the ScrollView a content area that's at most 720pt wide and anchored to the left. SwiftUI's `ScrollView` sizes its scroll-tracking area to the content's max width, so the vertical scroller pinned itself to **column 720 from the left edge** of the pane — looking like a scrollbar floating mid-screen on any window wider than ~750pt — and the rest of the detail pane was an empty gap to the right of the card. ## The fix One extra frame: ```swift .frame(maxWidth: 720, alignment: .leading) // card stays 720pt .frame(maxWidth: .infinity) // wrapper fills width ``` The inner frame keeps the readable column at 720pt (so line lengths don't get unreadable on a wide window). The outer frame's `.infinity` is what makes the ScrollView's content area span the full detail pane width; default `.center` alignment puts the 720pt card in the horizontal middle. Now the vertical scroller sits flush against the right edge of the detail pane — the System Settings / Xcode preferences look. ## Scope - **macOS only** — change is inside `macOSContent`, called from `formContent` only on `#if os(macOS)`. iOS `iOSFormContent` and tvOS layouts are untouched. - **Layout-only** — no behavioral change. Verified visually; per CLAUDE.md guidance, the existing structural assertions (`testSettingsShowsRegionPicker`, `testSettingsShowsDebugInfo` — both checking the accessibility identifiers are present and findable) still cover the contract this view exposes to tests. - iOS / macOS / tvOS all build clean. Branch is now 69 commits ahead of `origin/feature/native-macos-target`.

Commit `ab69fa2` lands on `feature/native-macos-target`. ## What was failing Running `xcodebuild test -scheme MovieSwiftMac -destination 'platform=macOS'` failed every test before any test method even ran, with: ``` The bundle "MovieSwiftMacTests" couldn't be loaded. dlopen ... code signature ... not valid for use in process: mapping process and mapped file (non-platform) have different Team IDs ``` Same symptom on `MovieSwiftMacUITests` ("Test crashed with signal kill before establishing connection" — the bug I'd flagged as "environmental" earlier was actually this). ## Why | Target | Code-signing | |---|---| | `Film-O-Matic.app` (host) | `ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME = YES`, `CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Automatic`, signs with `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = 27ZDER873F` | | `MovieSwiftMacTests.xctest` | `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED = NO`, `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY = "-"` — unsigned | | `MovieSwiftMacUITests.xctest` | same | Hardened runtime + Library Validation refuses to `dlopen` an unsigned `.xctest` into a properly-signed host process. I found the likely cause of the 400. Let me explain quickly, then I'll ask about the rest of the scope before going wide. **What's causing the 400 on Discover:** Tapping Discover triggers `FetchRandomDiscover` with `DiscoverFilter.randomFilter()` and `DiscoverFilter.toParams()`. The bug is at `DiscoverFilter.swift:74` + `:54`: ```swift params["page"] = "\(DiscoverFilter.randomPage())" // line 74 // where: static public func randomPage() -> Int { return Int.random(in: 1..<20) // line 54 } ``` It picks a random page from 1–19 **without first knowing how many pages the query actually has**. TMDB's `/discover/movie` returns **HTTP 400** when `page > total_pages`. For obscure year+sort combinations (especially `vote_average.asc` of an old year), there can be fewer than 19 pages — so any unlucky pick of, say, page 15 with year=1952 + sort=vote_average.asc triggers a 400. It's flaky-by-design. **Fix path** for the 400 itself: do a two-phase request — fetch page 1 first, read `total_pages` from the response, then pick a random page in `[1, total_pages]`. (Or fall back to page 1 if 400.) Now I want to be sure about the rest of the scope before I burn a bunch of effort:

Here's where things landed. ## What the failure actually was The skipped `testMyListsCustomListExists` looked like a missing accessibility identifier, but the real cause was two layers deep: 1. The macOS custom-list row is `.onTapGesture`-driven (not a `Button`), so SwiftUI merged its inner `Text` away — no amount of `.accessibilityElement`/identifier on a plain HStack surfaced it. 2. Even after forcing an explicit accessibility leaf, the row stayed absent from the tree because it lived in a **`LazyVStack`** — on macOS, a LazyVStack's lazily-created rows never acquire an accessibility identity even once they're laid out on-screen. The create *button* surfaced (Button), the gesture-row didn't. I confirmed the store was correctly seeded (`count=1` via a temporary diagnostic), which ruled out a data problem and pointed at the view layer. ## The fix (PR [#28](https://github.com/scottdensmore/MovieSwiftUI/pull/28)) - **My Lists (macOS):** `LazyVStack` → eager `VStack` (fine for user-curated lists of dozens, and it's an actual VoiceOver reachability fix, not just a test hack), plus `.accessibilityRepresentation { Button(list.name) … }` on the row so it surfaces as `myLists.customList.<id>`. - **Discover (macOS):** added the "Undo last dismiss" button to the empty state, gated on the same `DiscoverUndoState.canUndo` policy the iOS path uses. - Both previously-`XCTSkip`'d tests are re-enabled and now assert the real journeys (title clears then restores on undo; row carries the seeded name). ## Verification so far - `./scripts/lint.sh`: 0 violations - Both re-enabled macOS tests pass; neighboring My Lists tests still pass (no `VStack` regression); iOS builds - `code-reviewer` pass run pre-PR — applied the policy-object gate, strengthened both tests, documented the VoiceOver divergence, dropped a redundant label Two cleanups along the way worth …

Description states what/why/how-tested. 7. **Green CI is the merge gate** — the required checks are `package-tests`, `ios-tests`, `ios-tests-ipad`, `mac-tests`, `tvos-tests`; SwiftLint + CodeQL should also be green.
